title.value: Towards a unified a theory of value and cognitive maps in the Prefrontal Cortex

abstract.value: Although the Prefrontal Cortex is known to play a pivotal role in both value-based decision-making and schema learning, the frameworks for each remain largely distinct. By extending recent mechanistic understanding of cognitive maps in PFC to reward-based decision-making tasks, we demonstrate that PFC value responses are necessary for navigating the state-space of the task. Meta-trained RNNs are shown to learn internal value representations that act as control signals for the routing of activity within the network, consistent with the influential Miller \& Cohen hypothesis of PFC as an executive controller. This work builds towards a unifying theory of value and schema in PFC, and offers a mechanistic understanding of meta-reinforcement learners, both biological and artificial.
